findings.title: [P1] Restrict post-login redirects to safe same-origin paths
findings.body: When `returnUrl` is derived from user input, `location.assign` accepts external, protocol-relative, and executable-scheme URLs. An attacker can redirect authenticated users to a phishing site or potentially execute a `javascript:` URL in the page context. Validate the target and permit only intended same-origin paths.

findings.title: [P1] Stop writing issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body: `recordIssuedToken` passes the credential verbatim to `console.log`. In deployments that retain or aggregate console output, anyone with log access can recover and replay live tokens. Audit only non-sensitive metadata or a non-reversible identifier.

findings.title: [P3] Preserve the fallback for whitespace-only cached names
findings.body: For a cached value containing only whitespace, `trim()` produces `""`, but nullish coalescing does not select `"Anonymous"`. The function therefore returns an empty display name rather than its established fallback.

findings.title: [P1] Stop writing issued tokens to the audit log
findings.body:
Calling `recordIssuedToken` with a live session or bearer token writes the credential verbatim through `console.log`. In environments that collect console output, anyone with log access can recover and reuse the token to impersonate its holder.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict login return URLs to validated same-origin paths
findings.body:
`location.assign` accepts absolute and protocol-relative URLs, so passing an attacker-controlled value such as `https://attacker.example` redirects the authenticated user off-site. This creates an open redirect whenever `returnUrl` originates from a request/query parameter.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restrict post-login redirects to safe same-origin URLs
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` is attacker-controlled, `location.assign` accepts external and executable schemes such as `https://evil.example` or `javascript:...`, enabling phishing or script execution in the authenticated page context. Previously navigation was fixed to `/dashboard`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Stop writing issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body:
Every token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is emitted in plaintext through `console.log`. In environments that retain or aggregate console output, anyone with log access can recover and replay still-valid tokens, causing account or service compromise.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
